::: {#def-permutation-distribution}
#### Permutation distribution

Let $y = (y_1, \ldots, y_n)$ hold the observed values,
with the first $n_1$ entries belonging to group 1 and the rest to group 2,
and let $T(y)$ be a [test statistic](inference.qmd#def-test-statistic)
computed from the data and the group assignment.
Let $S_n$ be the set of all $n!$ permutations of $\set{1, \ldots, n}$.
The **permutation distribution** of $T$ is the distribution of $T(y_\pi)$
when $\pi$ is drawn uniformly from $S_n$ and $y$ is held fixed.
It puts probability $1 / n!$ on each relabeling $y_\pi$, so for every $t$

$$\Pr_\pi\paren{T(y_\pi) \ge t} \eqdef \frac{1}{n!} \sum_{\pi \in S_n} \indic{T(y_\pi) \ge t}.$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#exm-permutation-distribution}
#### The permutation distribution of six expression values

Take gene 3 in the Khan data, and keep the first three samples from tumor class 2 and the first three from class 4.
The test statistic is the absolute value of
[Welch's t statistic](basic-statistical-methods.qmd#def-two-sample-t-test).
Only $\binom{6}{3} =$ `r choose(6, 3)` relabelings differ in which values form group 1
(the other $3! \times 3!$ permutations within each group give the same statistic),
so all of them can be listed:

```{r}
#| label: permutation-distribution-toy
#| code-fold: false
toy <- rbind(
  head(khan_pair[khan_pair$tumor_class == 2, ], 3),
  head(khan_pair[khan_pair$tumor_class == 4, ], 3)
)
y_toy <- toy$gene_3
abs_welch_t <- function(y, in_group1) {
  x1 <- y[in_group1]
  x2 <- y[!in_group1]
  abs(mean(x1) - mean(x2)) / sqrt(var(x1) / length(x1) + var(x2) / length(x2))
}
group1_choices <- combn(6, 3)
t_toy <- apply(
  group1_choices, 2,
  function(idx) abs_welch_t(y_toy, seq_along(y_toy) %in% idx)
)
t_observed_toy <- abs_welch_t(y_toy, seq_along(y_toy) %in% 1:3)
data.frame(
  group_1 = apply(group1_choices, 2, paste, collapse = " "),
  statistic = t_toy
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(statistic)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

The statistics come in equal pairs,
because swapping the two groups gives the same absolute value.
The observed statistic is `r round(t_observed_toy, 3)`, the value of the relabeling `1 2 3`.
:::
